text:
Five friends – Asha, Ben, Cora, Dylan and Ella – each chose a different locker code from 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24.

• Ella’s code is higher than Cora’s.
• Ben’s code is 6 more than Asha’s.
• Dylan’s code is a multiple of 8.
• Cora’s code is 3 more than Asha’s.

Which statement must be true?
explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

text:
To win a science prize, a student must:
1. Submit an original experiment report, and
2. Give a short presentation to the judges.

Sam submitted an original report but did not win the prize.

Which conclusion is valid?
options: Sam must have failed the presentation
Sam may have given a presentation; the rules only state what is required, not that it is sufficient
Sam did not submit an original report
explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

An electric scooter may be moved by a motor while a bicycle is moved by pedalling

At existing kiosks most items brought in were successfully repaired after owners had planned to discard them
Some residents prefer to buy new items

Maya may or may not have handed in the draft on time
Maya did not hand in the draft
No one who was late received feedback

options: The probability of two red is higher than two green
The probability of two blue equals the probability of two green
The probability of two green is higher than two red
It is impossible to draw two of the same colour

options: It mistakes a regular sequence for a causal relationship
It is based on a false premise about roosters

The number of shops that sell it

You draw one fruit from the box labelled “Apples & Oranges” and it is an apple.

explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

text: Which of the following statements is logically equivalent to “If it is a square, then it is a rectangle”?
options: If it is a rectangle, then it is a square
If it is not a rectangle, then it is not a square
If it is not a square, then it is not a rectangle
explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

text: A cube is painted red on all sides and then cut into 27 smaller equal cubes (3×3×3).\n\nHow many of the small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

text:
Two statements are given:
1. All roses are flowers.
2. Some flowers fade quickly.

Which conclusion can be drawn?
options: None of the above conclusions definitely follow
explanation: Review the information in the question and compare each answer choice. A detailed worked solution is not yet verified for this item.

text: All members of the astronomy club study the sky. Some members of the astronomy club also play chess. Which conclusion must be true?
options: Every chess player studies the sky
Some people who study the sky play chess
No astronomy club member dislikes chess
Everyone who studies the sky joins the club
explanation: Those club members who play chess are people who study the sky and play chess; the other claims go beyond the premises.

text: A town proposes planting trees near bus stops because this will make waiting more comfortable during hot weather. Which assumption is most necessary?
options: All travellers prefer trees to shelters
Trees can provide shade at the bus stops
Bus stops have no roof anywhere
Every day in the town is hot
explanation: The argument relies on trees being able to provide shade or comparable relief where people wait; the other claims are unnecessary.

text: After a school introduced a reading hour, library borrowing increased. A teacher concludes the reading hour caused the increase. Which information most weakens the conclusion?
options: A new borrowing competition began in the same week
explanation: The borrowing competition is an alternative cause of the increase, making the single-cause conclusion less certain.

text: Lena finished before Omar but after Priya. Noah finished after Omar. Who finished first among these four?
explanation: The ordering is Priya, Lena, Omar, Noah.

text: If the alarm is armed, the red light is on. The red light is off. What follows?
explanation: By contraposition, if an armed alarm always has a red light on, an off light means it is not armed.

text: A student says: “Every champion I interviewed practises daily, so practising daily guarantees becoming a champion.” What is the main flaw?
options: It assumes all champions are the same age
It confuses a characteristic of champions with a guarantee of success
It does not state a training location
It ignores the meaning of the word daily
explanation: Observing that champions practise does not prove everyone who practises will become a champion.

text: A council says more people will cycle if a protected bicycle lane is built. Which finding best supports the prediction?
options: Most bicycles are painted dark colours
A survey finds many residents avoid cycling mainly because they fear traffic
explanation: Safety from traffic is a specific barrier that a protected lane could address.

text: Every wooden toy in a box is painted. Some painted toys are wooden. Which statement must be true?
options: There is at least one painted wooden toy
All toys in the box are wooden
explanation: The premise that some painted toys are wooden directly guarantees at least one painted wooden toy.

text: Which number should come next? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
explanation: These terms are n(n+1) for n=1 through 5; the next is 6×7=42.

text: Exactly one of Arun and Bella is telling the truth. Arun says: “Bella is lying.” Bella says: “We are both lying.” Who is telling the truth?
explanation: Arun is truthful: Bella’s claim that both are lying is false because Arun tells the truth. If Bella were truthful, her statement that she herself lies would be impossible.

text: A ticket is valid only if it has been stamped. Rosa has a valid ticket. What must be true?
explanation: Stamping is a necessary condition of validity, so a valid ticket must be stamped.

text: A principal says, “Replacing the old lights will lower our electricity bill because the new lights use less power.” Which additional fact is most relevant to estimating the savings?
options: The colour of the light switches
How many hours the lights are used
explanation: Electricity consumption depends on both power and time used, so the hours are essential to estimating savings.

text: Seed is to tree as egg is to _____.
explanation: A seed can develop into a tree, just as an egg can develop into a bird.

text: Three notices say: (1) Every gate in the park is locked at night. (2) The east gate is a gate in the park. (3) The east gate is unlocked tonight. Which combination creates a contradiction?
explanation: Statement 1 applies to the east gate only when statement 2 identifies it as a park gate. Statement 3 then contradicts its required locked status.

text: A prize is awarded to the tallest person in a group. Mira is taller than Jo and shorter than Kai. Which additional statement proves Kai wins?
options: There are exactly three people in the group
explanation: With exactly Mira, Jo and Kai in the group, Kai exceeds both and must be tallest.

text: A sports club notices fewer injuries after it changed training times and introduced new warm-ups. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: The warm-ups alone caused the reduction
The time change alone caused the reduction
The decrease occurred after both changes, but the cause is not established
explanation: Because both changes happened together, the evidence does not isolate either as the cause.

text: A password must contain exactly one digit and exactly two letters, and the digit must be last. Which password follows the rule?
explanation: AB7 contains exactly two letters followed by exactly one digit.

text: A number is greater than 20, less than 40, divisible by 3 and even, but not divisible by 9. Which number could it be?
explanation: 24 is even and divisible by 3, but not by 9. 36 is divisible by 9; 27 and 39 are odd.

text: A company claims its reusable bottle is the best because it is the most expensive. Which evidence would best test the claim?
explanation: Performance and durability are relevant to quality, while price alone is not sufficient evidence.

text: No penguins in the sanctuary can fly. Pippa is a penguin in the sanctuary. Which statement must be true?
explanation: The general rule applies to every sanctuary penguin including Pippa.

text: A robot faces north, turns 90° clockwise, then 180°, then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction does it face?
explanation: North → east → west → south.

text: A train leaves every 15 minutes starting at 8:00 am. A traveller arrives at the platform at 8:37 am. If trains run exactly on schedule, when is the next departure?
explanation: Departures are 8:00, 8:15, 8:30, 8:45; the next after 8:37 is 8:45.

text: “The new playground is safer because fewer injuries were reported this month.” Which fact makes this comparison least convincing?
options: The new playground uses blue paint
The playground was closed for most of the month
explanation: Far fewer opportunities to use the playground would naturally reduce total injuries without showing lower risk per visit.

text: Five boxes are arranged left to right. The red box is immediately left of the blue box. The green box is immediately right of the blue box. Which statement must be true?
options: There are no other boxes between red and green
explanation: Their order is red, blue, green. Thus red is left of green; there is actually one box (blue) between them.

text: A shop reports that 60% of its sales on Saturday were made online. Which statement must follow?
options: More than half of Saturday sales were online
More than half of all weekly sales were online
Online shoppers spent more per sale
The shop sold fewer products on Sunday
explanation: Sixty per cent exceeds half, but the information concerns only the share of Saturday sales, not other days or spending.

text: Every amber token is round. No round token is wooden. Which statement must be true?
explanation: All amber tokens belong to the round set, which is disjoint from the wooden set.

text: A scientist claims that a new plant food makes beans grow taller. Which test provides the strongest evidence?
options: Measure only the tallest plant after feeding it.
Compare two groups with the same light and water, changing only the plant food.
Ask gardeners whether they like the food.
Compare beans fed the food outdoors with unfed beans indoors.
explanation: Only the first design controls relevant differences while changing the proposed cause.

text: Four runners finish a race. Ben finishes before Cleo. Ada finishes after Cleo. Dev finishes before Ben. Who must finish first?
explanation: The clues force Dev before Ben before Cleo before Ada.

text: A museum found that more visitors came on rainy days than sunny days. Its manager concluded rain makes people visit museums. Which point most weakens the conclusion?
options: The museum has a gift shop.
Rainy days in the records were mostly weekends, while sunny days were mostly weekdays.
explanation: Weekends are a competing explanation for attendance; the comparison does not isolate rain.

text: If a light is green, the gate opens. The gate is open now. What can be concluded?
options: The light could be green or another condition could have opened the gate.
The light has never been green.
explanation: Green is sufficient to open the gate but not stated to be necessary.

text: Three boxes contain exactly one coin each: one gold, one silver and one bronze. Box A is not gold. Box B is bronze. Which coin is in Box C if Box A is silver?
explanation: B is bronze and A is silver, leaving gold for C.

text: A code shifts each letter forward by two positions in the alphabet, wrapping from Z to A. What is the code for WAX?
explanation: W→Y, A→C and X→Z, giving YCZ.

text: A school canteen is open only if a supervisor is present. Today no supervisor is present. Which conclusion follows?
options: A supervisor is on the way.
The canteen serves no food on Mondays.
explanation: Being open requires a supervisor. Without one, the canteen cannot be open.

text: Nina says, “All red kites fly high.” Omar replies, “I saw a kite flying high, so it must have been red.” What is wrong with Omar’s reasoning?
options: He confuses a consequence with its possible cause.
He assumes red kites cannot fly.
He says there are no other colours.
He proves every kite is red.
explanation: Flying high could occur for kites of other colours; the rule gives only one direction.

text: Some library books are mysteries. All mysteries have a yellow sticker. Which statement must be true?
options: All library books have yellow stickers.
Some library books have yellow stickers.
No library book is a mystery.
Every yellow-stickered book is a mystery.
explanation: At least one library book is a mystery and mysteries all have yellow stickers.

text: A teacher observes students who eat breakfast score higher in a quiz. Which fact makes it hardest to claim breakfast caused the scores?
options: The quiz was on a Tuesday.
Students who eat breakfast also tend to sleep longer, and sleep can affect concentration.
explanation: Sleep is a plausible confounding variable affecting both breakfast habits and quiz performance.

text: A robot faces north. It turns 90° clockwise, then 180°, then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction does it face?
explanation: North → east → west → south.

text: In a competition, every entrant who reached the final had won at least one earlier match. Which statement must be true?
options: A finalist won at least one earlier match.
Everyone who won an earlier match reached the final.
explanation: This restates the necessary requirement for being a finalist without reversing it.

text: A shopkeeper says, “These shoes are popular, so they must be the most durable.” What assumption does the claim rely on?
explanation: The inference depends on popularity being evidence of durability.

text: Every square card is blue. Some blue cards are striped. Which statement must be true?
explanation: Only the first statement is directly guaranteed; the striped cards need not be squares.

text: The sign reads: “Visitors may enter the garden if they have a ticket.” Which conclusion is justified?
options: Everyone who enters bought a ticket.
Anyone without a ticket is definitely forbidden.
A ticket is sufficient for permission to enter.
explanation: The sign grants permission to ticket holders but does not explicitly exclude others.

text: A report says 80% of 100 survey responses preferred buses to taxis. Which conclusion follows?
options: 80% of the whole town prefers buses.
No one in the survey prefers taxis.
explanation: 80% of 100 responses is 80; the sample alone does not establish facts about the whole town.

text: A door has two switches: it opens if exactly one switch is on. Switch A is on. What should switch B be for the door to open?
explanation: With A on, exactly one is on only when B is off.

text: A timetable shows lessons in this order: Music before Art; Science after Art; Maths before Music. Which subject must occur before Science?
explanation: The order is Maths → Music → Art → Science.

text: A club accepts a member only if they are at least 10 years old. Jo is nine. What follows?
options: Jo must already be a member.
Jo cannot be accepted under that rule.
explanation: Being at least 10 is necessary for acceptance; Jo does not satisfy the condition.

text: Lila says, “The park is safer since the new lights were installed, because fewer accidents were reported.” Which additional fact would best support this argument?
options: Visitor numbers stayed similar and reports were collected the same way before and after installation.
A different park also has lights.
explanation: Comparable exposure and reporting reduce alternative explanations for the observed change.

text: The sequence of symbols is ▲ ● ● ▲ ● ● ▲ … . What is the tenth symbol?
explanation: The repeating block has three symbols ▲ ● ●. Positions 1,4,7,10 are ▲.

text: A recipe says “Use butter only if the oven is preheated.” Butter was used. What must be true if the instruction was followed?
explanation: Only if states a necessary condition: using butter requires the oven to be preheated.

text: All three robots are painted either red or blue. Exactly two are red. Which statement must be true?
options: At least one robot is blue.
explanation: Of the three robots, exactly two are red and the remaining one is blue.

text: A student argues: “This book has won an award, so everyone will enjoy it.” What is the main flaw?
options: It assumes an award guarantees universal enjoyment.
explanation: An award is not evidence that every individual will like the book.

text: A locked chest opens when BOTH keys are turned. Key A is turned and the chest stays shut. Which observation is consistent with the rule?
options: The rule guarantees it cannot open.
The chest opens with no keys.
explanation: If both keys are required, an unturned B explains why turning A alone leaves the chest shut.

text: An advert claims a drink improves memory because three famous athletes recommend it. What evidence would best test the claim?
options: How often the advert is displayed.
Results from a well-controlled memory study comparing drink users and non-users.
explanation: A controlled comparison tests the claimed effect rather than popularity or celebrity endorsement.

text: If a parcel is fragile, it gets a red label. A parcel has no red label. What must follow if the rule is always followed?
explanation: The contrapositive of fragile → red is not red → not fragile.

text: There are three cards showing 2, 4 and 6. Exactly one card is chosen. What is the strongest conclusion from “the chosen number is greater than 3”?
options: The chosen card is either 4 or 6.
All cards are even and greater than 3.
explanation: The cards greater than 3 are 4 and 6; neither is specified individually.

text: A map shows directions: the bakery is east of the library; the clinic is north of the bakery. Which direction is the library from the clinic?
explanation: From the clinic go south to the bakery, then west to the library.

text: A school introduced free fruit at lunchtime. Afterwards, the number of late students fell. What information would most help decide if the fruit caused the change?
options: The colour of the fruit baskets.
Whether the school also changed its late-arrival policy at the same time.
explanation: A simultaneous policy change could explain fewer late arrivals independently of fruit.

text: Four friends each have a different pet: cat, dog, fish or bird. Alex has the fish. Blair does not have the cat or bird. Casey has the bird. What pet does Drew have?
explanation: Alex fish, Casey bird; Blair can only have dog, leaving cat for Drew.

text: All people wearing badges may enter a hall. Which extra information would let us conclude Kai may enter?
options: Kai is standing near the door.
Kai knows someone with a badge.
explanation: The general permission applies to badge wearers; knowing Kai wears one lets us apply it.

text: A student says, “No triangles are circles, and some road signs are triangles.” What must be true?
options: Some road signs are not circles.
explanation: The road signs that are triangles cannot also be circles.

text: A water clock fills a marked section every 5 minutes. At 2:00 it is at mark 1. At what time is it at mark 6, assuming it never stops?
explanation: Moving from mark 1 to mark 6 requires five intervals, each five minutes: 25 minutes.

text: A gallery has the rule: “Either the blue room OR the green room is open today, but not both.” The blue room is closed. What must be true?
explanation: Exactly one room must be open, so if blue is closed, green is open.

text: Which finding would most weaken the claim “Students who play chess have better grades because chess improves concentration”?
options: Chess players already had higher grades before they began playing chess.
Some students play chess at lunch.
Chess is played on a board.
explanation: Pre-existing grade differences suggest selection rather than improvement caused by chess.

text: Four numbered envelopes have consecutive whole-number labels. Their sum is 34. What is the largest label?
explanation: Four consecutive integers summing to 34 are 7, 8, 9, 10.

text: A poster says “All morning classes begin before 11 am.” A class begins at 10:30 am. What can we conclude?
options: It cannot be a morning class.
It must be a morning class.
It might be a morning class, but the poster does not establish that.
explanation: The poster states a requirement for morning classes, not a definition of every class before 11 am.

text: A science team tested a paper plane once and found it flew 10 metres. They claim it always flies 10 metres. What would improve their claim most?
options: Give the plane a new name.
Ask one friend whether the plane looks fast.
Repeat the test many times under comparable conditions and record the distances.
explanation: Repeated measurements show whether one result was typical or due to chance.
